name: Alternators and generator heads
summary: Machines that turn spinning into electricity: car and truck alternators, and AC generator heads.
uses: Wind, water or pedal generators (car alternators need gearing: about 1,500+ rpm)
Charging a 12V battery bank from an engine
Replacing the head on a broken generator
identify: Car alternators are finned aluminium cases with a belt pulley, bolted to the engine; most have a built-in regulator and rectifier and give 13.5–14.5V DC. Generator heads are the round end of a portable or standby generator and give 120V or 230V AC, enough to kill.
test: Spin it by hand: the bearings should be smooth and quiet. Connected to a battery, with the field (warning light) terminal fed, a drill-driven car alternator should push the battery above 13.5V.

decay.note: Lasts. Brushes and bearings wear but can be replaced.
